script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A bustling coffee shop in the heart of a metropolitan city. Customers chatter, baristas work behind the counter, and steam rises from a latte.

NATHAN (30s, brooding) sits alone at a table, staring at a laptop. The cafe door swings open. In walks EMMA (20s, cheerful), carrying a tray of pastries. She spots Nathan and walks over, setting down the tray.

EMMA
(smiling)
Hey, Nathan. I brought you something.

NATHAN
(looking up, surprised)
Emma, hi. Thanks.

Emma takes a seat across from Nathan.

EMMA
You've been coming here every day for a week now. I figured I'd offer you some company.

Nathan looks down at his laptop again.

NATHAN
I'm just trying to finish this script.

EMMA
That's what you've been telling yourself every day?

Nathan sighs.

NATHAN
It's more than that. It's something important. I need to get it right.

EMMA
What's stopping you?

Nathan hesitates, then leans back in his chair.

NATHAN
Forgiveness. Or lack thereof.

EMMA
(leaning forward)
You mean from someone else, or yourself?

Nathan looks up, surprised by her insight.

NATHAN
Both, I suppose.

INT. COURTHOUSE - DAY

Nathan and Emma sit in the courtroom as the judge reads the sentence for a man named JASON (30s, stoic), who stole from Nathan years ago.

JUDGE
(to Jason)
You will serve three years in prison.

Nathan's eyes fill with anger and disappointment.

INT. PARK - DAY

Emma and Nathan sit on a bench in the park. Nathan is deep in thought, while Emma tries to engage him in conversation.

EMMA
(pointing to a dog playing nearby)
Look at that dog. He doesn't hold a grudge. He doesn't care that someone took his favorite stick. He just plays and moves on.

NATHAN
(shrugs)
That's easy for a dog. Humans aren't as forgiving.

EMMA
But why not be? It doesn't do any good to hold onto anger and resentment.

Nathan sighs and looks at her.

NATHAN
I wish I could. But sometimes the past is too heavy to let go.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - NIGHT

Nathan and Emma sit in the coffee shop, their conversation more animated than before.

EMMA
What if you could talk to him? Face to face?

Nathan pauses, then nods.

NATHAN
Maybe that's what I need to do.

INT. JASON'S APARTMENT - DAY

Nathan arrives at Jason's apartment. He knocks, and Jason answers, surprise on his face.

JASON
(stunned)
Nathan? What are you doing here?

NATHAN
(looking Jason in the eye)
I came to talk. To forgive.

Jason steps back, unsure.

JASON
I stole from you, Nathan. I can't undo that.

NATHAN
(shaking his head)
No, you can't. But you can make amends. You can change.

Jason hesitates, then nods.

JASON
I can try.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Nathan and Emma sit in the coffee shop once more, their conversation lighter than before.

EMMA
You look relieved.

NATHAN
(smiling)
I am. It feels good to let go of the past.

EMMA
(smiling back)
I'm proud of you, Nathan.

Nathan looks at her, then at his laptop.

NATHAN
I think I'll be able to finish my script now.

INT. COURTHOUSE - DAY

Three years later, Nathan and Emma sit in the same courtroom as Jason, who has just been released from prison. Nathan approaches him, a handshake and a smile exchanged between the two men.

NATHAN
(looking at Jason)
Welcome back, Jason. I'm glad we had this chance to talk.

JASON
(grinning)
Me too, Nathan. Me too.

FADE OUT.
